\(c\) can be used to combine both vectors and scalars into large vectors

title: 2  R Basic
text:
2.10 Recycling Rule of Vectors

c(1, 2, 3, 4) + c(1, 2)

[1] 2 4 4 6

# c(1, 2, 3, 4) + c(1, 2, 1, 2)

\[
    \begin{bmatrix}
        1 \\
        2 \\
        3 \\
        4
    \end{bmatrix} +
    \begin{bmatrix}
       1 \\
       2
    \end{bmatrix} \xrightarrow{recyle}
    \begin{bmatrix}
        1 \\
        2 \\
        3 \\
        4
    \end{bmatrix} +
    \begin{bmatrix}
       1 \\
       2 \\
       1 \\
       2
    \end{bmatrix} \xrightarrow{add}
    \begin{bmatrix}
        2 \\
        4 \\
        4 \\
        6
    \end{bmatrix}
\]

text:
3.2 Cumulative Summaries
These functions doesn’t have na.rm argument (NA remove)

[1]   1   2   6  24 120 720

cummin(1:10) # min(1,n)...
